content.text:
Most likely two phases are present: Sr2CoSbO6 (mp-1218837) and Li2Nb4ZnO12 (mp-756793). I simulated only three candidates (Sr2CoSbO6, Ca3SiO5 and Li2Nb4ZnO12) and matched peak positions by eye, with no quantitative fit. I ruled out three others from their cell sizes alone. That leaves Zn2Co3O8 and Li3CoO3 unchecked and is why confidence is moderate.

- **Sr2CoSbO6 (mp-1218837):** its simulated pattern has a two-peak cluster near 30–32° (about 45–50 and 100). The observed pattern has the same at 30.0–30.4° (45–50) and 31.3–31.8° (100). The next strong peaks also line up: about 41.6°, 45.5° and a pair near 51°, plus a weak peak near 18.7°. The observed peaks seem slightly shifted from the simulation, but they follow it closely.
- **Li2Nb4ZnO12 (mp-756793):** Sr2CoSbO6 cannot explain the observed peak at 23.0° (about 42). Li2Nb4ZnO12's strongest simulated peak sits at about 23.15°. Scaled to 42, its second-strongest peak (relative 38) predicts about 16 near 33°. The observed peak at 33.5° is 13–15. That fits, but I placed the simulated peak by counting array indices, so its position is approximate.
- **Ca3SiO5 (mp-37657):** simulated, but its main peaks fall at about 29.4°, 32.2–32.7° and 34.3°. The observed pattern does not match this.
- **Ruled out from the cell alone:**
  - BaSrYBiO6 would put its main peak near 29.2°, not 31.8°.
  - KInO2 would show a low-angle peak near 14°.
  - Na2NiO2 would show one near 10.6°.

  None of these is in the data.
